:::{#def-one-se-rule}
#### One-standard-error rule

Let $\candproc{1}, \ldots, \candproc{\ncand}$ be candidate [fitting procedures](#def-fitting-procedure),
each [at least as flexible](#def-flexibility) as the one before,
cross-validated on a training set $\trainset$ with the same folds,
and let $\candproc{\icand^*}$ be the one with the smallest
[cross-validation estimate](#def-cv-estimate-indexed).
The **one-standard-error rule** chooses the smallest $\icand$
whose estimate is within one [fold-based standard error](#def-cv-se-indexed)
of the smallest:

$$
\cvestoff{\nfolds}{\candproc{\icand}}{\trainset} \le \cvestoff{\nfolds}{\candproc{\icand^*}}{\trainset} + \cvseoff{\nfolds}{\candproc{\icand^*}}{\trainset}.
$$ {#eq-one-se-rule}

Source: [@hastie2009elements, sec. 7.10.1; @james2021islr2e, sec. 6.1.3].

:::
